paras: The Greensburg jail fire destroyed the wooden jail at Greensburg, Louisiana, on the night of October 31 or November 1, 1888, killing its only prisoner, a Black youth held on a charge of horse stealing. The cause of the fire was not reported, and the story circulated nationally as a one-sentence wire brief.
According to the Washington Evening Star, the jail was "an old wooden structure recently condemned." Its sole occupant at the time was an unnamed "negro boy" accused of horse stealing.

A dispatch dated Greensburg, November 2, stated that the jail "was burned last night" and that the prisoner "perished in the flames." The Evening Star placed the fire on Wednesday night and was less certain of the outcome, saying the boy "is supposed to have perished." None of the reports says how the fire began or names anyone as responsible.
No report of an inquest, an investigation or the recovery of the prisoner's remains appears in the coverage.

The wire dispatch ran on November 2 in papers from Connecticut to Delaware and Minnesota, and a week later in Dakota, mostly under plain headlines such as "Jail and Occupant Burned" and "Perished in a Burning Jail." The St. Paul Daily Globe instead headed it "A Negro Thief Cremated," presenting the accusation as fact.

A "Southern Gleanings" digest printed in the West Tennessee Star on November 9 reported that the young prisoner "was cremated." The same digest ran the next day in the St. Landry Democrat of Opelousas, the only Louisiana paper found carrying the story.

Reports differ on the date, with the Evening Star giving Wednesday night and reprints of the wire carrying datelines of November 1, 2 and 3 over the words "last night." They also differ on the certainty of the death, which the wire stated outright and the Evening Star only supposed.

reader.title: Greensburg jail fire
bases: The papers report a jail fire in which the sole prisoner died, but none names a cause, a mob or any other actor, and one describes the building as an old, condemned wooden structure (A1, A2, A5).

The prisoner was reported to have died in the fire, though one report says only that he was 'supposed' to have perished (A1, A2). No report says the fire was set, by whom, or why, so nothing shows a killing by a group of three or more under a pretext of justice, race or tradition (A1, A2, A5).

A wire dispatch and a separately worded Washington item agree that the Greensburg jail burned with its only prisoner, a Black boy charged with horse stealing, inside, though the Washington item hedges on his death (A1, A2).
